terms.gloss: apply for, seek (a post); stand for (office)
terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation, with an accusative
evidence: Cic. Att. 1.1.2: nēmō est enim ex iīs quī nunc petunt
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “to apply or solicit for an office, to be a candidate for office”: cōnsulātum petere (Cic. Phil. 2.76). The same verb serves for any post or place one asks to be given.

terms.gloss: give in one’s name (as a candidate, a volunteer)
terms.grammar: verb phrase; profiteor, second conjugation, deponent

terms.comment: From the whitened toga (toga candida) of those standing for office.

evidence: Cic. de Or. 2.280 (Lewis & Short): repulsam ferre
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “the class. technical phrase” for losing an election; see fail.

phrases.latin: nēmō est enim ex iīs quī nunc petunt quī, sī in nostrum annum reciderit, firmior candidātus fore videātur
phrases.english: For of those now standing there is no one who, if his election falls in my year, would look like a stronger candidate.

phrases.latin: quattuor et vīgintī fermē annōs nātus, professus sē petere, in superiōre unde cōnspicī posset locō cōnstitit
phrases.english: About twenty-four years old, he declared that he was standing, and took his place on higher ground where everyone could see him.
Are you applying for that job?
to be defeated, to lose an election
phrases.source: Cic. de Or. 2.280 (Lewis & Short s.v. repulsa)
